A Satirical Royal Reunion

The latest episode of **SNL U.K.** opened with a sketch that imagines a contentious family gathering at the Sandringham Estate. The cold open brings together Prince William (Freddie Meredith) and Kate (Annabel Marlow) with Prince Harry (Jack Shep) and Meghan (Ayoade Bamgboye), only to reveal former Prince Andrew (George Fouracres) as the mastermind behind the invitation.

> “This place brings back so many memories,” Bamgboye’s Meghan says to Harry, referencing a fictional anecdote about a grand‑parent asking if she was related to Beyoncé.

The dialogue continues with playful jabs: William is mock‑named “Prince Ginger Pubes,” while Kate teases Meghan about her former role on *Suits*. Harry retorts that Meghan “doesn’t do anything anymore,” a line that mirrors ongoing media narratives about the couple’s public activities.

Prince Andrew’s Unexpected Cameo

The sketch takes a darker turn when a character portraying Prince Andrew, played by George Fouracres, appears with an “evil laugh” and claims responsibility for the invitation. He references real‑world legal controversies, stating, “Didn’t you hear the good news? The search warrants were unlawful! That means it doesn’t count. I’m innocent!”

King Charles (Larry Dean) and Queen Camilla (Emma Sidi) intervene, delivering a line that blends satire with criticism of the monarchy’s historical legacy: “You’re arrogant, you’re entitled, you represent an outdated institution founded on centuries of war, tax evasion and slavery.” The sketch ends on a conciliatory note, with Charles offering Andrew “one drink… and the million pounds I’ll give you for the rest of your life,” underscoring the absurdity of the imagined reconciliation.

Context and Background

SNL U.K., the British spin‑off of the long‑running American sketch show, frequently uses its platform to lampoon public figures. The royal family has been a recurring target, especially after the 2023 interview with Harry and Meghan that sparked renewed debate about the monarchy’s relevance. Prince Andrew’s legal battles over his association with Jeffrey Epstein have also kept him in the public eye, making his inclusion in the sketch both timely and provocative.

Audience Impact and Reception

While the Variety article does not provide viewership data, early social‑media reactions suggest the sketch resonated with viewers who appreciate sharp political satire. Some commentators praised the boldness of featuring Andrew, whereas others warned that the humor could alienate royal‑sympathetic audiences. The episode was hosted by Danny Dyer with musical guest Sasha Keable, adding further star power to the broadcast.

Uncertainties and What to Watch

The sketch’s reception may influence future SNL U.K. content. It remains unclear whether the show will continue to spotlight the royal family with the same intensity or shift focus based on audience feedback.
